title: Father's orchestra, lakefront dances and band members
summary: His father led an orchestra playing dances around the lake and Bucktown, with Vic Gaspard, cousin Albert Gabriel and others; his father is named as Martin Manuel Gabriel.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Did he say if he played dance music or if he played classical or opera or anything?

No, he played nothing but jazzical music. You understand? Through the can-can-finish. He used to play waltz or for a drill. You know all of them, they played that kind of music. Do you remember, was that a B-flat cornet or? It was. It was a B-flat trumpet. A trumpet? Not a trumpet. It was a real cornet. Real cornet. Yeah, short cornet. The trumpets didn't come out until later years. And that was a B-flat horn, B-flat cornet. They called them trumpets around about, when it was the way in the late years of the 20s. When it won, I think. Yeah, when they took up the trumpet. When he was still teaching you music, was he still playing? He was still playing. Do you remember where or with who he was playing? Well, he had his own orchestra, you see, and he used to play out there all around the lake. Like called Over the Ride. It was out there around the Spanish boat, Millenway. Then there's another place, this big restaurant here, out here in Bunktown. That's what I remember in the morse. He used to give dances too out at Bunktown. Bunktown is right at the foot of the seawall. That's Bunktown. Right where the seawall started. In the west end there, huh? Yeah, right where the seawall started. Right where the mile line club. That's the start of the seawall. Do you remember any of the musicians that were playing with your father that time? Well, that was called the old Gatsby. He used to play bass. No, it was the trombone player. Vic was that? Vic Gatsby. Vic Gatsby. And, well, I used to use my cousin, dude, he used to call me, Albert Gabriel. He was the clarinet player. Dude, dude. Albert Gabriel. He was the clarinet player. And, Jonathan Sear, he was the guitar player. And, basically, I was called the old man Alphonse Gatsby. Alphonse Gatsby. Alphonse Gatsby. Alphonse Gatsby. Was that any relates to Vic and the... Well, it's supposed to be cousins. See, we never did get that straight. Yeah. It was supposed to be just the cousins. Yeah, it was related. I was trying to tell you. Dude, that's the one I was trying to tell you. Was playing B-flat Landry and the Holy Ghost Band. I was playing E-flat Landry. Remember, I couldn't remember his name. I didn't remember him. But that's who was playing, because his father was playing trumpet too. And his father, Big Landry, Pinchback, Two Rows. That's the name I was trying to remember when I was talking to you. Did you say your father taught you? Well, yeah, he showed us how to... Man and two? Man and two. He took man on the drum. That's what made man switch off on the drum to the clarinet. Because he didn't like that token of the drum. Yeah, two halves of the car. Two halves of the car. So, he got off the drum and he was clarinet. I got the release place in the drum. It's at the drum.
Did you tell us your father's name, his first name? His first name is Martin. Martin.
